headline: AI agents can autonomously buy data with gasless prepaid on Base
summary: A new endpoint allows AI agents to pay for APIs using a single USDC deposit on Base, enabling gasless, instant transactions without repeated on-chain fees.
details: AI agents can now autonomously pay for APIs, addressing the challenge of frequent on-chain transactions. A new live endpoint on Base, utilizing x402 and gasless prepaid, allows agents to manage API payments end-to-end in USDC.
Traditional HTTP 402 endpoints require an on-chain transaction for every API call, incurring gas fees and latency. This is inefficient for AI agents making hundreds of calls.

The x402.obolpay.xyz solution introduces a prepaid balance: agents deposit USDC once, then pay per call with off-chain signed vouchers. This eliminates on-chain transactions, gas fees, and ensures instant payments.

Key benefits include a free preview to evaluate APIs before payment, and gasless prepaid for unlimited cheap calls after a single deposit. This saves context tokens with delta delivery, providing only new data.
Agents also receive signed receipts for verifiable proof-of-purchase. A freshness SLA ensures stale data is auto-refunded to their balance, guaranteeing value.

The system integrates with Claude or any MCP agent by adding the MCP server. This provides tools for agents to discover, preview, purchase, manage balance, top-up, spend gaslessly, and verify receipts autonomously.

Developers can try the endpoint at https://x402.obolpay.xyz, access the client at curl https://x402.obolpay.xyz/client.py, and view the manifest at /.well-known/x402. The system is built on x402 and Base.

headline_marked: [[Android 17's App Bubbles]] integrated into taskbar for seamless multitasking
headline: Android 17's App Bubbles integrated into taskbar for seamless multitasking
summary: Google's latest Android update brings a desktop-like window management experience to foldables, minimizing apps to the taskbar.
details: Android 17's stable build is now available, and it introduces a significant multitasking enhancement for foldable devices: App Bubbles.
These App Bubbles allow users to open almost any application in a floating window. Once minimized, they reside in the taskbar, similar to how windows are managed on a desktop operating system.
Unlike on regular phones where minimized apps appear as floating bubbles on the screen's edge, foldables like the Pixel 10 Pro Fold integrate these minimized apps directly into the taskbar.
This implementation offers a cleaner interface, making the multitasking experience feel more akin to using a desktop.
Users can easily jump back into a minimized app by tapping its icon on the taskbar. To dismiss an app entirely, it can be dragged to the bottom of the screen.
Android 17 currently supports up to five active App Bubbles simultaneously. While accessing the taskbar on a full-screen app requires a slight upward swipe, the benefit is a less cluttered display.
This feature is considered a major multitasking improvement for Android, offering a quick and glanceable way to manage multiple applications.
While other manufacturers offer their own multitasking solutions, Google's App Bubbles on foldables are praised for their seamless integration and user-friendly approach.
